newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ICI appeals over Helix pesticide decision.
newsitem.headline: ICI appeals over Helix pesticide decision.

text.p: Chemicals group ICI Australia Ltd said on Monday it had lodged an appeal over a Federal Court decision last week relating to the pesticide Helix.
ICI said it was appealing the court's decision to dismiss claims made by cattle producers in a class action against the states of New South Wales and Queensland.

The Federal Court last Wednesday found that ICI had in some cases breached its duty of care over the manufacture and distribution of the pesticide, which cattle producers in the two states alleged contaminated their stock.
The court dismissed a similar claim against the New South Wales and Queensland governments.

More than 450 producers were seeking over A$100 million in compensation following the discovery of chemical residue in cattle fed cotton trash sprayed with Helix during drought conditions between 1989 and 1994.
The discovery led to a beef contamination scare and a temporary freeze on some exports, which the producers said cost them both domestic and export sales.

ICI said last week it had complied with regulatory requirements and industry standards when it registered Helix for use on cotton crops, and believed responsibility for the economic losses did not lie with it.
